chapters.name: Solid State

formulas.name: Density of Unit Cell Formula
formulas.description: [M in g/mol, a in cm, ρ in g/cm³, NA = 6.022 × 10²³]

keyPoints: Schottky Defect: Equal number of cations and anions missing; lowers density; high CN and similar sizes (NaCl, KCl, CsCl, AgBr).
Frenkel Defect: Dislocation of smaller cation into interstitial site; density remains unchanged; large size difference (ZnS, AgCl, AgBr, AgI).
Note: AgBr exhibits both Schottky and Frenkel defects.
Metal Excess (F-Centres): Trapped electrons in anionic vacancies impart color and paramagnetism (yellow NaCl, pink LiCl, violet KCl).

chapters.name: Liquid Solutions

formulas.name: Raoult's Law (Volatile Liquid Mixture)
formulas.latex: p_{total} = p_A + p_B = p_A^\circ x_A + p_B^\circ x_B = p_B^\circ + (p_A^\circ - p_B^\circ) x_A

formulas.name: Relative Lowering of Vapor Pressure
formulas.latex: \frac{p_1^\circ - p}{p_1^\circ} = i x_2 \approx i \left(\frac{n_2}{n_1}\right) = i \left[\frac{w_2 M_1}{M_2 w_1}\right]

formulas.name: Elevation of Boiling Point
formulas.latex: \Delta T_b = T_b - T_b^\circ = i K_b m = i \left[\frac{1000 K_b w_2}{M_2 w_1}\right]

formulas.name: Depression of Freezing Point
formulas.latex: \Delta T_f = T_f^\circ - T_f = i K_f m = i \left[\frac{1000 K_f w_2}{M_2 w_1}\right]

formulas.name: Osmotic Pressure
formulas.latex: \Pi = i C R T = i \left(\frac{w_2}{M_2 V}\right) R T
formulas.description: Best colligative property for determining molar mass of biomacromolecules.

formulas.name: Van 't Hoff Factor (Association)
formulas.description: K4[Fe(CN)6]: n = 5 ⇒ i = 1 + 4α. Acetic acid dimerizes in benzene (n = 2) ⇒ i = 1 - α/2.

keyPoints: Non-Ideal Positive Deviation: ΔHmix > 0, ΔVmix > 0, forms minimum boiling azeotropes.
Non-Ideal Negative Deviation: ΔHmix < 0, ΔVmix < 0, forms maximum boiling azeotropes.

chapters.name: Electrochemistry

formulas.name: Equilibrium Constant & Free Energy
formulas.latex: \log K_c = \frac{n E^\circ_{cell}}{0.0591}, \qquad \Delta_r G^\circ = -n F E^\circ_{cell} = -2.303 RT \log K_c

formulas.name: Molar Conductivity
formulas.description: Kohlrausch's Law: Λm° = ν+ λ+° + ν- λ-°

formulas.name: Faraday's Laws of Electrolysis
formulas.latex: w = z Q = z I t = \left[\frac{M}{n F}\right] I t, \qquad \frac{w_1}{w_2} = \frac{E_1}{E_2}

keyPoints: Dry Cell: Anode: Zn → Zn2+ + 2e-; Cathode: MnO2 + NH4+ + e- → MnO(OH) + NH3; E ≈ 1.5 V.
Mercury Cell: Anode: Zn(Hg) + 2OH- → ZnO + H2O + 2e-; Cathode: HgO + H2O + 2e- → Hg + 2OH-; E = 1.35 V (constant voltage).
Lead Storage Battery (Discharge): Pb + PbO2 + 2H2SO4 → 2PbSO4 + 2H2O; E ≈ 2 V per cell (12 V battery = 6 cells in series).
H2-O2 Fuel Cell: 2H2 + O2 → 2H2O; Efficiency ≈ 70%.

formulas.name: Zero Order Kinetics
formulas.description: Units of k: mol L⁻¹ s⁻¹

formulas.name: Arrhenius Equation
formulas.latex: k = A e^{-E_a/RT} \implies \log\left(\frac{k_2}{k_1}\right) = \frac{E_a}{2.303 R} \left[\frac{T_2 - T_1}{T_1 T_2}\right]
formulas.description: Plot of log k vs 1/T has Slope = -Ea / (2.303 R) and Intercept = log A.

chapters.name: Coordination Compounds & d/f-Block Elements

formulas.name: Crystal Field Splitting
formulas.description: Octahedral: t2g lowered by 0.4Δo, eg raised by 0.6Δo. Tetrahedral: e lowered by 0.6Δt, t2 raised by 0.4Δt.

formulas.name: Crystal Field Stabilization Energy (CFSE)
formulas.description: Strong field (Δo > P): Low spin. Weak field (Δo < P): High spin.

keyPoints: Spectrochemical series: I- < Br- < SCN- < Cl- < S2- < F- < OH- < C2O42- < H2O < NCS- < edta4- < NH3 < en < CN- < CO.
Chromate & Dichromate Preparations: 2CrO42- (yellow) + 2H+ ⇌ Cr2O72- (orange) + H2O
Cr2O72- + 14H+ + 6e- → 2Cr3+ + 7H2O (E° = +1.33 V). Oxidizes Fe2+→Fe3+, I-→I2, H2S→S, Sn2+→Sn4+.
Permanganate Preparations: 2MnO4- + 5C2O42- + 16H+ → 2Mn2+ + 10CO2 + 8H2O (Acidic)
2MnO4- + H2O + I- → 2MnO2 + 2OH- + IO3- (Alkaline/Neutral)
In acidic medium, MnO4- → Mn2+ (n-factor = 5). In faintly alkaline/neutral medium, MnO4- → MnO2 (n-factor = 3).

chapters.name: Organic Chemistry Reactions
keyPoints: SN1: 2 steps via carbocation intermediate; racemisation; reactivity: 3° > 2° > 1° > CH3X (Benzylic ≈ Allylic > 3°); polar protic solvents.
SN2: 1 step via transition state; 100% Walden inversion; reactivity: CH3X > 1° > 2° > 3°; polar aprotic solvents (acetone, DMSO, DMF).
Aldol Condensation: Aldehydes/ketones with ≥ 1 α-H in dil. NaOH ⇒ β-hydroxyaldehyde/ketone → α,β-unsaturated carbonyl.
Cannizzaro Reaction: Aldehydes with NO α-H (HCHO, C6H5CHO) in 50% conc. KOH ⇒ disproportionation into alcohol + carboxylate salt.
Rosenmund Reduction: RCOCl + H2 →(Pd/BaSO4) RCHO.
Stephen Reaction: RCN + SnCl2/HCl → RCH=NH →(H3O+) RCHO.
Étard Reaction: Toluene + CrO2Cl2/CS2 → Benzaldehyde.
Gattermann-Koch: Benzene + CO + HCl →(anh. AlCl3/CuCl) Benzaldehyde.
Clemmensen Reduction: >C=O →(Zn-Hg / conc. HCl) >CH2.
Wolff-Kishner Reduction: >C=O →(NH2NH2, KOH/glycol, Δ) >CH2.
Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky (HVZ): R-CH2-COOH + X2/red P → R-CH(X)-COOH.
Gabriel Phthalimide: Prepares pure 1° aliphatic amines (aromatic amines cannot be prepared).
Hoffmann Bromamide Degradation: RCONH2 + Br2 + 4NaOH → RNH2 (1 less carbon) + Na2CO3 + 2NaBr + 2H2O.
Carbylamine Test (Isocyanide): RNH2 / ArNH2 + CHCl3 + 3KOH → RNC (foul odor) + 3KCl + 3H2O. (1° amines only).
Hinsberg Test: C6H5SO2Cl (1° amine ⇒ soluble in alkali; 2° amine ⇒ insoluble in alkali; 3° amine ⇒ no reaction).

Phenol Reactions: Kolbe's synthesis (→ Salicylic acid with CO2/NaOH); Reimer-Tiemann (→ Salicylaldehyde with CHCl3/NaOH via :CCl2 carbene intermediate); Coupling with diazonium salt (→ p-hydroxyazobenzene orange dye at pH 9–10).
